images.title: Every family counted: the mean is 5.22
images.purpose: Shows the family size data as stacks of dots, with the balance point near 5.22, not 6.5.
images.composition: Plain white background, the main object large and centred with wide empty margins, no scenery, no characters, no extra decoration. One dot plot centred in the frame with a balance triangle under the line.
images.exact_structure: One horizontal number line with 8 unlabelled tick marks for the family sizes 3 to 10; only the end ticks show the numerals 3 and 10. Teal (#0072B2) dots, all the same size, stacked above the ticks: 3 dots above 3, 11 above 4, 9 above 5, 7 above 6, 3 above 7, 1 above 8, 1 above 9, 1 above 10; 36 dots in all. A filled reddish purple (#CC79A7) triangle under the line at about 5.22, a little to the right of 5, with the label mean ≈ 5.22. A small grey (#6B7280) mark at 6.5 under the line, struck through with a grey cross and labelled 6.5. The axis title family size sits under the line.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: Each value counts as many times as it occurs, so the tall stack at 4 pulls the mean down to about 5.22.
images.description: Shows the family size data as stacks of dots, with the balance point near 5.22, not 6.5.
images.context: Sizes 3 to 10 occur 3, 11, 9, 7, 3, 1, 1, 1 times: 36 students, total 188, mean 188 divided by 36.
images.teaching_notes: The struck out 6.5 is the wrong method: averaging the distinct sizes.

image_decisions.why: Stacks make it visible that frequent values weigh more in the mean.
